summary: Enterprise customer unable to update routing policies (control plane config write failures, 500s)
description:
Issue summary
- Zenlytics (enterprise) cannot create/update routing policies in the Redwood control plane. UI and API requests fail with 500 errors.

Customer impact
- Customer is blocked from: (a) updating routing policy weights, (b) pinning model version for a new rollout, (c) adding a new fallback region.
- Live inference traffic continues to serve, but customer cannot make policy changes and is stuck on last-known-good policy config.
- Customer indicates an urgent business need to shift traffic due to performance issues on a model variant; inability to change policy is time-sensitive.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2026-01-29 16:05: Customer reports in shared Slack + opens support ticket.
- 16:12: Support reproduces via API; escalated to SRE + Platform Control Plane.
- 16:25: Incident channel created; initial mitigation/workaround attempted.
- 17:10: Root cause narrowed to control plane config write path (DB transaction + audit log write) under specific payload size/shape.
- 18:05: Hotfix deployed to us-east control plane API.
- 18:18: Customer confirms ability to update policy via API; Console still intermittently fails due to retry logic.
- 19:10: Console retry/backoff change rolled out; errors resolved.

How to reproduce
1) PUT /v1/routing/policies/{policy_id} with policy payload >= ~200KB (customer has many routes + per-route conditions).
2) Observe HTTP 500 and no policy update.

Observed errors
- API response:
  - HTTP 500
  - body: {"error":"internal_error","message":"failed to persist policy config"}
  - response headers include x-request-id (examples below)

Customer-provided request IDs (x-request-id)
- 01JH2K6Q7S2W9N7D2K6D9M0FQK
- 01JH2K7A2F0S8Y3K1C1C5WQ8TX

Support reproduction notes
- Repro confirmed from Redwood side using customer-scoped token (impersonation) in us-east.
- Console (ops + customer) surfaced generic error toast; Network tab shows 500 from /console-api/routing/policy.

Initial triage / hypotheses
- Auth/RBAC rejected writes? (ruled out: requests pass authz and fail in persistence step)
- Control plane DB contention / transaction timeout? (partially true)
- Audit log write path failure causing overall transaction rollback? (confirmed)

Investigation notes (engineering)
- Primary oncall: Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park) with SRE support (Rafael Mendes).
- Findings:
  - A recent change increased audit log payload size by including full pre/post config diffs for routing policies.
  - For large policy payloads, the audit log row exceeded a DB row/TOAST threshold and triggered a slow write; combined with a strict transaction timeout caused rollback.
  - Control plane API returned a generic 500 without a structured error code, which slowed down triage.

Mitigation / workaround provided to customer
- Temporary workaround offered at 16:40 UTC: split policy update into smaller incremental PATCH operations (per-route) to reduce payload size.
- Customer attempted; reduced but did not eliminate failures (still hit the audit log path for some operations).

Fix implemented
- Hotfix (18:05 UTC):
  - Changed audit logging to store a summarized diff (hash + top-level fields) for routing policy writes; full payload stored in object store asynchronously when needed.
  - Increased transaction timeout specifically for the policy write path with bounded retry on serialization failures.
- Console (19:10 UTC): adjusted retry/backoff and surfaced a more actionable error message including request-id.

Customer confirmation
- 18:18 UTC: Customer confirms policy updates succeed via API.
- 19:22 UTC: Customer confirms Console UI updates succeed; no further 500s observed.

Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping (for Reliability Program)
- Proposed classification (v1 taxonomy): Control plane outage > Config write/CRUD failures.
- Primary owner: Platform Control Plane.
- Secondary/consulted: SRE (incident process + comms), Smart Routing (validation layer), Observability (dashboards/alerts for error rate).
- Note: This ticket is being used as a concrete example in the ownership mapping table to keep "control plane config writes" distinct from "routing/fallback misbehavior" and "auth/RBAC failures".

Requested follow-ups
- Add structured error code for config write failures (e.g., CONTROL_PLANE_CONFIG_WRITE_FAILED vs INTERNAL_ERROR) and emit as metric label (low-cardinality).
- Add an alert for elevated 5xx on control-plane write endpoints, segmented by endpoint group (read vs write).
- Document known limit guidance: recommend policy size limits + how to structure complex routing policies.

Customer communications
- Rachel Kim provided customer-facing update cadence (every 30 min) in shared Slack; avoided attributing specific DB internals, focused on mitigation and restoration timeline.

Attachments / links
- Incident channel: #incidents (internal) referencing INC-2026-01-29-CP-CONFIG-WRITES
- Shared customer channel: #zenlytics-redwood (internal reference)
- Grafana (internal): Control plane API 5xx + latency spikes in us-east during incident window

Next update
- Close ticket after 48h monitoring window and confirm no recurring write failures; keep one-week watch alert for elevated write failures on policy endpoints.
